findings.title: Cache devices only after admission succeeds
findings.body: tagDeviceUI caches the device before CreateOrUpdateDevice checks the limit. When the store returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, that cache entry remains for 29 minutes. A second request with the rejected device ID therefore returns nil from the cache check, and Anonymous.Authenticate grants access without enforcing the limit. Simply retrying bypasses the restriction. Populate the cache only after a successful store operation, and test repeated requests from a rejected device.

findings.title: Make device admission atomic across requests
findings.body: CountDevices and the subsequent upsert run in separate database sessions without synchronization. With one slot remaining, concurrent requests from different new devices can all observe a count below the limit and then all insert successfully. Those excess devices subsequently qualify for updates and can remain admitted indefinitely. Serialize the count-and-admit operation at the database level so the limit also holds across Grafana instances.

findings.title: Do not treat a missing device ID as successful admission
findings.body: Anonymous authentication now relies on TagDevice to reject requests beyond the limit, but TagDevice returns nil immediately when X-Grafana-Device-Id is absent. Consequently, even with the configured limit exhausted, a caller can omit this client-controlled header and receive an anonymous identity for API requests without being counted or checked. Limited anonymous access needs an admission path for requests without a device ID rather than treating them as admitted.

findings.title: Make the device limit configurable through environment overrides
findings.body: The new device_limit key is read from the raw INI section but is not added to conf/defaults.ini. Grafana's normal environment-override pass visits keys already present in the loaded configuration, so setting GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_DEVICE_LIMIT alone leaves this value at 0 and silently disables enforcement. Add the key to the defaults or read it through SectionWithEnvOverrides, with a test covering an environment-only configuration.
